app.title: TwistScope
app.summary: A person sets two crystal layers and a twist angle to simulate the bilayer's diffraction pattern and its real-space moiré, then reads the derived quantities beside them. In the measure mode they load an image: an upload, a built-in example, or the current simulation sent over with noise added. They say whether it is a real-space micrograph or a diffraction pattern and give its scale if they know it. The tool finds the spots, splits them into the two layers and reports the twist angle with an uncertainty, a confidence flag and, when the scale is given, the closest matching material.

task.text: Measure the twist angle between two stacked crystal layers, with an uncertainty and the likely material, from a diffraction pattern or a micrograph, and simulate the expected pattern for comparison.

data.text: A single microscope image, either a real-space micrograph of a lattice or an electron diffraction pattern, plus a simulated pattern generated from chosen lattice parameters and a twist angle.
data.item: one image of a twisted bilayer, either in real space or as a diffraction pattern

stage.text: analysing diffraction or microscope images of a sample, before reporting its twist angle

mechanism.text: In the simulate tab, controls for the layers, twist angle and model settings redraw a diffraction screen and a real-space screen side by side, with derived readouts below. The measure tab runs spot detection on an uploaded, example or sent-over image, marks the detected spots by layer on the input and on its Fourier transform, and shows the angle with its uncertainty, a confidence pill and the material match.

field.text: twist-angle measurement of 2D bilayers from electron diffraction and microscopy, in materials science

workflow.name: estimate a quantity with its uncertainty from an image, checked against a simulation

steps.step: simulate what the data should look like for chosen parameters
steps.here: Pick the bottom and top layer materials and set the twist angle with a slider or number box. Adjust the double-scattering strength, spot size and contrast, and choose whether spots are marked by layer. The diffraction and real-space screens and the readouts (moiré period, spot distances, mismatch, brightness ratio) update live.

Drop or choose a PNG or JPG, which is cropped to its centre square and resampled to 512 × 512. Or load one of two generated examples with a known answer, or send the current simulation over as a noisy diffraction pattern or moiré image.

steps.step: describe the input so it is read correctly
steps.here: Choose real-space image or diffraction pattern. Then give the image width in nm (real space) or the camera scale in 1/nm per pixel (diffraction), switch on stretch correction for figures copied from papers, and pick a material hint for images that show only the moiré.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Measure finds the spots and locates the centre from pairs of opposite spots. It corrects the stretch so the rings are circular, folds spot directions modulo 60° and splits them into two layer groups. Real-space images are Fourier-transformed first. The detected spots are circled by layer on the input or on its transform.

steps.step: read the result with how sure it is
steps.here: The result shows the twist angle ± the spot scatter and a 'Clean measurement' or 'Check by eye' pill. It also gives the method used, the measured lattice constant with the closest material, a moiré cross-check, the spots used, and notes on what is missing.

distinctive: The simulator can send its own pattern to the measurer with noise added, so the true answer is known and the measurement can be checked against it
Spot directions are folded modulo 60° (hexagonal symmetry) and clustered into two groups, so the angle comes from the gap between groups and the uncertainty from the scatter within each
The pattern centre is found from midpoints of opposite spot pairs, so it works even when a beam stop hides the centre
Uneven horizontal stretch in figures copied from papers is fitted and corrected by making the spot rings circular
The material is identified only when a physical scale is given, and lattices within about 3% are reported as ties
